version.changelog: v1.0.1: Multi-agent compatibility. SKILL.md updated to support Claude, Cursor, Codex, OpenClaw and any AI agent platform. Path references generalized with platform-specific examples.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: skill-quality-check
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is a comprehensive quality assessment framework designed to audit and score AI Agent Skills (SKILL.md files) based on best practices like conciseness and progressive disclosure. The instructions in SKILL.md and the supporting documentation in references/audit-rules.md are purely analytical and educational, focusing on optimizing token usage and trigger accuracy. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution was found; the included curl command is used strictly for fetching remote markdown files for analysis.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only audit tool whose requested actions and resources are coherent with its stated purpose (reading and evaluating SKILL.md files); it does not request credentials or install code.

dimensions.detail: Name and description claim an audit tool and the skill only needs to read SKILL.md files and related resources (examples, references). All declared/implicit capabilities (scanning directories, reading SKILL.md, fetching raw GitHub SKILL.md) align with an audit purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to locate and read SKILL.md files from user-specified and common platform locations and to optionally curl raw.githubusercontent.com for remote SKILL.md. This is expected for an auditor, but it means the agent will access files under home directories and may perform network fetches of remote SKILL.md. If you run the audit against sensitive skill directories, be aware the agent will read those files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no bundled executable code — instruction-only. That keeps disk/write risk low and matches the described functionality.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. The SKILL.md references common skill storage paths (for locating SKILL.md), which is appropriate for an auditor and does not request unrelated secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show always:false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not request permanent presence or elevated platform privileges. Nothing in the skill attempts to modify other skills or system-wide settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent and appears safe as an audit tool. Before running it: 1) Prefer supplying an explicit path to the SKILL.md you want audited instead of allowing broad directory scans, to avoid unintentionally exposing other local skills; 2) Be aware the audit suggests fetching SKILL.md via raw.githubusercontent.com — ensure you trust the remote repository before allowing network fetches; 3) Because the skill is instruction-only, it will act only insofar as the agent is permitted to read files or fetch URLs — review and control those agent permissions if you handle sensitive skill code. If you want stronger isolation, copy the target SKILL.md to a temporary location and audit that copy.
